note: Experimental submodule of cloudfront_purger adding cache-tag invalidation. Provides purger plugin id 'cloudfront_tags' (types tag/path/wildcardpath/everything; extends the base cloudfront purger, emitting #<hash> paths for tag invalidations) and a TagsHeader plugin (id 'cloudfront', header_name 'Cache-Tags') that builds the header via filter (purge_queuer_coretags blocklist) -> prioritize (entity tags, then _list, then other) -> hash (xxHash3 truncated to 6 hex chars). Config cloudfront_purger_tags.settings:cache_tag_header_name (default 'Cache-Tags') must match the distribution's CacheTagConfig HeaderName. Swappable services: CacheTagFilterInterface/CacheTagPrioritizerInterface/CacheTagsHashInterface. Medium reads the live header-name config; hard registers the cloudfront_tags purger in Purge (purge.plugins), verified against live config with NO AWS calls (parent stays disabled). Baseline restored (cache_tag_header_name='Cache-Tags', no purgers).

evals.prompt: What purger plugin does the CloudFront Purger Tags submodule add, and how is it different from the base cloudfront purger regarding invalidation types?
evals.expected_output: It adds the 'cloudfront_tags' purger which supports the tag invalidation type in addition to path, wildcardpath and everything. It extends the base cloudfront purger and, for a tag invalidation, sends a '#<hash>' path to CloudFront.

evals.prompt: How does CloudFront Purger Tags build the Cache-Tags header value from a response's Drupal cache tags? Describe the steps and how tags are shortened.
evals.expected_output: Three steps: filter (drop tags matching the purge_queuer_coretags blocklist), prioritize (entity tags like node:123 first, then _list tags, then other), then hash each tag with xxHash3 truncated to 6 hex characters. The results are comma-joined into the Cache-Tags header.

evals.prompt: For CloudFront Purger Tags to work, what must be configured on the AWS CloudFront distribution, and which Drupal config value must match it? Is there a tag limit to be aware of?
evals.expected_output: The distribution needs CacheTagConfig enabled with a HeaderName that matches cloudfront_purger_tags.settings:cache_tag_header_name (default 'Cache-Tags'). CloudFront stores at most 50 tags per cached object (plus size limits), which is why tags are prioritized and hashed.

evals.prompt: On this site the CloudFront Purger Tags cache-tag header has been given a non-default name. Inspect the live configuration and report the configured header name.

Register the tag-aware CloudFront purger (the one that supports cache-tag invalidation) with the Purge module on this site, so cache-tag invalidations go to CloudFront. Apply it to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: purge.plugins purgers contains an instance with plugin_id 'cloudfront_tags' (e.g. drush p:purger-add cloudfront_tags).
